annotation.kind: reconstruction of the format-derived threshold, row-specific power-of-two diagonal scaling, equation (3.4a), and its exact maximum-coefficient consequence

assumptions: The matrix dimensions m and n are positive.
The largest finite input- and accumulation-format values fmax and Fmax are positive, and theta is fixed to min(fmax,sqrt(Fmax/n)) as in (3.2).
Every row of A has positive explicit finite-maximum infinity norm, making the quotients in (3.4a) defined.
The exact-real model represents the source assumption that A, B, and C are stored in sufficiently high precision and that no range exception occurs before forward scaling or after inverse scaling.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P20 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P20 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p20_t1_power_two_row_scaling {m n : Nat} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real) (fmax Fmax : Real) (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n) (hfmax : 0 < fmax) (hFmax : 0 < Fmax) (hrow : forall i, 0 < p20InfNormVec (A i)) : let theta := p20ScalingThreshold n fmax Fmax; every selected row factor is a positive integer power of two satisfying (3.4a), every coefficient of p20LeftScaledMatrix theta A is bounded by theta, and every row has a coefficient strictly larger than theta/2
formal_statement.plain_language: For every nonzero row of A, construct the power-of-two diagonal factor prescribed by the paper using its format-derived theta, prove the exact interval (3.4a), and prove that the scaled row maximum lies in (theta/2,theta].

informal_proof: For each positive ratio theta/||A_i||_infinity, use the Archimedean adjacent-power theorem to select an integer exponent k with 2^k <= theta/||A_i||_infinity < 2^(k+1). Rearranging gives (3.4a). Bound every row coefficient by the explicit finite maximum and select a coefficient attaining that maximum to obtain the closed upper and strict lower scaled-row bounds.
informal_statement: The paper's complete row-side scaling selection from (3.1)-(3.4a): format-derived theta, positive power-of-two diagonal factors, and scaled-row maxima in (theta/2,theta].
